deadlines.label: The AI Act enters into force
deadlines.detail: Article 113: the Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal (12 July 2024). Entry into force is not the same as application: most rules apply later, see the dates below.

deadlines.label: Prohibited practices and AI literacy apply
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (a): Chapters I and II (general provisions including Article 4 AI literacy, and the Article 5 prohibitions) apply from 2 February 2025, except Article 5(1), points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b), which apply from 2 December 2026. Article 4 in its current wording (support the development of AI literacy) applies since Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force on 27 July 2026.

deadlines.label: Penalty rules apply
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (b): Chapter XII (penalties) applies from 2 August 2025. Breaking an Article 5 prohibition can be fined up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (Article 99(3)); breaches of other duties, including Articles 16, 26 and 50, up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3 % (Article 99(4)). For SMEs and start-ups the lower of the two amounts applies (Article 99(6)); for SMCs the lower amount applies to the fines of paragraphs 4 and 5 (Article 99(6a)).

deadlines.label: Digital Omnibus on AI enters into force
deadlines.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026, published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026, enters into force on the third day after publication (its Article 4). From this date Articles 102 to 110 apply (Article 113, third paragraph, point (d)), and the amended provisions that have no later date, such as Article 4 and Article 4a, apply. It moves the high-risk dates, adds two prohibitions from 2 December 2026 and adds a transition period for Article 50(2).

deadlines.label: General date of application
deadlines.detail: Article 113, second paragraph: the Regulation applies from 2 August 2026, except where Article 113 sets another date. This includes Chapter IV (Article 50 transparency duties) and Article 101 (fines for general-purpose AI model providers). Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 (high-risk classification, requirements and obligations) no longer apply from this date: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 moved them, see the high-risk entries.

deadlines.label: New prohibitions on non-consensual intimate imagery and child sexual abuse material apply
deadlines.detail: Article 5(1), points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b), inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744: AI systems that generate or manipulate realistic intimate images, video or audio of an identifiable person without that person's consent, or child sexual abuse material within the meaning of Directive 2011/93/EU. They apply from 2 December 2026 (Article 113, third paragraph, point (a)).
